slides.title: The AI Lemons Problem
slides.subtitle: How AI adoption can unravel prediction markets

slides.frametitle: AI can improve prediction while undermining market viability
slides.claim: Higher AI penetration widens spreads and drives out uninformed traders.
evidence: The informed share of order flow rises with AI adoption
Uninformed participation is endogenous to the spread
slides.takeaway: The market can collapse even as conditional prediction improves.

slides.frametitle: Prediction markets need counterparties, not information alone
slides.claim: The paper makes participation, rather than price accuracy alone, the central margin.
evidence: Liquidity traders and recreational users sustain two-sided order flow
Their willingness to trade falls when spreads become costly
slides.takeaway: Market composition determines whether information aggregation remains possible.

slides.frametitle: AI adoption creates a self-reinforcing adverse-selection spiral
slides.caption: AI adoption raises informational asymmetry, spreads, and uninformed exit.
slides.takeaway: Participation feedback turns asymmetry into possible collapse.

slides.frametitle: The model combines informed trading with endogenous participation
items: Binary prediction contract with state V in {0,1}
AI-informed traders have superior predictive ability
Uninformed traders have heterogeneous participation values z
Competitive market makers price orders conditional on direction

slides.frametitle: Pricing and participation form a fixed-point problem
definitions: F(s): share of uninformed traders priced out
slides.meaning: A wider spread reduces participation and makes order flow more informative.

slides.frametitle: More AI makes every order more revealing to the market maker
slides.claim: The gap between buy probabilities across states equals the AI penetration rate alpha.
evidence: AI traders buy when V = 1 and sell when V = 0
Uninformed traders trade only when z exceeds the spread
slides.takeaway: Higher alpha raises adverse-selection pricing pressure directly.

slides.frametitle: Higher AI penetration shifts the spread schedule toward collapse

slides.frametitle: AI penetration above the threshold eliminates active equilibrium
slides.statement: If alpha > 2 z-bar, no active equilibrium exists and the collapsed equilibrium is unique.
slides.intuition: The minimum AI-induced spread exceeds the strongest non-informational participation value.

slides.frametitle: The gradual phase is wider spreads and fewer ordinary participants
slides.claim: Before collapse, equilibrium spreads rise and participation falls with AI penetration.
evidence: The spread operator is increasing in s and α
slides.takeaway: The collapse theorem is the endpoint of a continuous deterioration mechanism.

slides.frametitle: AI rents are transfers, while participation creates baseline surplus
slides.claim: In the baseline welfare criterion, AI does not create direct productive surplus.
evidence: AI rents equal spread losses borne by uninformed traders
Market makers earn zero expected profit
Real surplus comes from non-informational participation values
slides.takeaway: Private profitability and social value need not move together.

slides.frametitle: Participation-based welfare declines with AI penetration
definitions: The integral captures surviving participation value
slides.meaning: AI reduces welfare by shrinking the set of traders who remain active.

slides.frametitle: Private AI adoption can exceed the planner's optimum
slides.statement: With non-negative adoption costs and the baseline welfare criterion, the planner chooses the lowest feasible adoption level.
slides.intuition: Adopters capture private rents but do not internalize the participation externality imposed on other traders.

slides.frametitle: Market design can target participation rather than price accuracy
items: Participation subsidies reduce the effective cost of trading
AI adoption taxes reduce privately chosen adoption
Public information can reduce the AI informational edge
AMM liquidity support addresses the analogous withdrawal spiral

slides.frametitle: The collapse mechanism survives imperfect AI and alternative institutions
items: Imperfect AI replaces α with effective informed intensity
Heterogeneous quality preserves the adverse-selection feedback
Dynamic persistence creates path dependence and hysteresis
AMMs and multi-market settings retain the core participation force

slides.frametitle: The theory yields testable predictions but not current-market evidence
slides.claim: The paper identifies empirical implications rather than claiming that prediction markets have already collapsed.
evidence: AI exposure should predict wider spreads
Wider spreads should reduce less-informed participation
Order flow should become more concentrated in informed traders
slides.takeaway: Whether real markets are near the threshold remains an open empirical question.

slides.frametitle: The headline is a trade-off between local efficiency and institutional survival
slides.takeaway: AI may improve price discovery while destroying the participation base that makes price discovery possible.
